key_insight: Scaling Representation Autoencoder (RAE) decoders on a frozen high‑capacity semantic encoder (SigLIP-2) enables diffusion transformers to produce higher-fidelity, large-scale freeform text-to-image outputs, but dataset composition (web, synthetic, text-rendered) is critical for text and attribute fidelity.
problem_solved: How to scale text-to-image diffusion models efficiently while preserving semantic fidelity and readable text in generated images using a reusable representation backbone.
method: Freeze a high-capacity semantic encoder (SigLIP-2) and scale RAE decoders to operate in its high-dimensional latent space.
Train on a mixed corpus (web imagery, synthetic data, text-rendered examples) to broaden visual concepts and improve text handling.
Integrate the RAE latent space with a diffusion transformer conditioning pipeline for freeform text prompts, leveraging the frozen encoder to improve training stability and reuse.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable pathway to build high-quality T2I models by decoupling representation learning from generative decoding—reducing retraining cost and improving sample fidelity and text accuracy for downstream applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen SigLIP-2 encoder → RAE latent space → diffusion transformer decoder pipeline.
Dataset composition pie chart: web vs synthetic vs text-rendered data and their impact on metrics.
Scaling curve: sample fidelity / text accuracy vs decoder/model scale.

paper_title: Scaling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers with Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Shengbang Tong, Boyang Zheng, Ziteng Wang, Bingda Tang, Nanye Ma
